text: After a week the colony's walls hold marks from five different mark defs: the inspect pane lists Tag_A, Tag_B, Tag_C, Stencil_A and Stencil_B. On the wall, Tag_B and Tag_C are the same lettering shape as Tag_A in green and orange, and both stencils are the same star shape in two colours. A player walking the corridor sees two shapes in five colours.
expect: reject: the player must see several visibly different kinds of mark, not recolours of one; five def names over two shapes in tints is the 'one def in six tints' false pass, whatever the def list says

text: The tester checks variety across three quicktest colonies. Colony one's walls hold only throw-ups, colony two's only tallies, colony three's only sigils. Each colony's own marks are one shape in several tints, but all three colonies together show three clearly different kinds.
expect: reject: the variety must be seen in one colony; spreading kinds across separate colonies while each colony's walls show recolours of one kind does not meet it

text: A colonist walks past the same mockery every hour for two days. It never shows two copies of the thought: the mood panel always shows a single 'mocked on the wall' line, but its timer resets to full on every pass, so the debuff never runs down while the colonist keeps using that corridor.
expect: reject: the mark may move mood at most once per day; a single thought renewed on every hourly pass is renewed many times a day, which keeps the effect up without a break, even though it never stacks

text: Over two in-game days of hourly passes, the colonist's mood thought from the mockery is renewed once each day, as intended. The social tab shows the colonist's opinion of the painter drop by 5 on day one and by another 5 on day two, once each day, never per pass.
expect: reject: opinion must change only once, on the first read; a daily renewed opinion drop is a second opinion change from the same mark

text: A colonist passes the same mockery 24 times a day for two days. Day one: one mood thought and one opinion drop toward the painter at the first pass, nothing more that day. Day two: the mood thought appears once more after the first one has expired; opinion of the painter does not move again.
expect: accept: mood moves at most once a day (once on each of the two days) and opinion moves only once, on the first read; a new thought on the second day is what 'at most daily' allows

text: Three in-game weeks in an ordinary colony of six. No colonist ever holds more than one graffiti thought at a time, each is -2 to -3, and each comes from a different mark as marks appear and get scrubbed. But on 19 of the 21 days every colonist carries some graffiti debuff, so the colony's mood sits about 3 lower than with graffiti switched off.
expect: reject: graffiti must make occasional stories, never a standing mood penalty; a small debuff every colonist carries almost every day is a tax even though no single thought is large and the source keeps changing

text: Over a week in an ordinary colony, a graffiti message arrives about every four hours: a new mockery, a tribute, a scrub, a reply, a clean freak's complaint. Every message describes a different event between named colonists, and none repeats.
expect: reject: a message every few hours is the message stream the leaf forbids; each message being a distinct story does not make about 40 a week 'occasional'

text: A three-week run of an ordinary colony counts Graffiti messages: four in total, well within the bar. The count covers messages only. Over the same weeks the raid-mark and raider-pressure letters number about ten a week, one each time a mark goes up or comes down.
expect: reject: messages and letters together must number few per week; counting only one kind is a named false pass, and ten letters a week is a stream

text: A three-week run of an ordinary colony of six with every graffiti setting on and no forcing. In those weeks nobody paints anything worth noticing, no mark draws a reaction, no letter or message arrives, and no colonist ever holds a graffiti thought. The tester calls it clean: no tax, no stream.
expect: reject: the player must see graffiti make occasional stories; a colony where graffiti produces nothing over three weeks shows no tax but none of the required stories either

text: An outdoor tally lasts ten days. It looks crisp for its first four days, then fades steadily over the next six and is gone on day ten. Under a roof the same tally lasts sixteen days with the same shape: crisp for the first 40%, then a long fade.
expect: reject: a mark must stay crisp for most of its life before it fades; crisp for 40% and fading for 60% is fading for most of its life

text: The kernel selftest passes: the fade curve holds full strength to 80% of a mark's weather days, then falls to zero, and roofed weather days exceed unroofed for every form. In game, a throw-up on an outer wall stays fully crisp right up to its last day and then disappears in a single tick; the drawn mark never uses the curve.
expect: reject: the mark must visibly fade before it goes; a correct curve the drawn mark never uses still gives a mark that pops out of existence, which the player cannot see fade

text: Colony and enemy tags weather as intended: crisp, then a visible fade, sooner outdoors. Raid exit tags, though, are flagged permanent so the raid's story stays on the wall, and the build notes say permanent marks are exempt from fading. Unscrubbed raid tags are still on the outer walls a year later.
expect: reject: weathering exists to bound raid marks and the pressure they carry; a build where raid marks never weather and so last forever is the failure case the leaf names, and the permanent exemption cannot be stretched to cover them

text: One colonist paints a vandal scrawl and a tally at each craft level. At Awful through Excellent the scrawl inspects uglier than the tally. At Masterwork and Legendary the craft bonus caps both at the same beauty, so the scrawl inspects exactly as pretty as the tally. At a glance the scrawl always looks worse.
expect: reject: when the same hand painted both, the scrawl must inspect as uglier at every craft that hand can roll; equal beauty at the top crafts means the stat stops agreeing with the picture there

text: A master artist's vandal scrawl hangs next to a tally painted by a colonist with art skill 1. The scrawl still looks rougher at a glance, but in the inspect pane the master's scrawl has higher beauty than the novice's tally.
expect: accept: the inspect requirement applies only when the same hand painted both; across different painters art skill may lift a scrawl's beauty, and the picture still shows the scrawl as the worse-looking mark

text: Faction A left three exit marks on the colony's walls, and a letter named A and pointed at one of them. A colonist scrubs the first of the three. The letter's effect ends right away: A's next raid comes at the same points and time as faction B's, while two A marks still stand on the outer walls.
expect: reject: A's raids must come sooner or larger while any A mark stands, and only the last mark gone lifts the push; lifting it at the first scrub while two marks remain ends the pressure early

text: A trader caravan of the Tribe passes an insult to the Tribe on the colony wall four times in one visit; goodwill drops once, on the first pass. Twenty days later a new caravan from the same faction visits, passes the same still-standing insult, and goodwill drops once more, then not again during that visit.
expect: accept: the limit is once per visit and never again from that wall during the visit; a new visit is a new read, and the drop did not recharge within either visit
